editorial.summary: David Choe joins Jim Rugg and Ed Piskor for a page-by-page reading of The Punisher #94–95, drawn by Frank Teran. The episode is direct craft genealogy: Choe names lessons in motion, bodies and composition, accepts a Slow Jams comparison, and describes Teran’s two-issue impact as a youthful career ideal. He also traces a childhood masculinity script through family and violent media, then explicitly revises it at 45 by distinguishing comic endurance from real bodies and describing discomfort with current violent work. Every graphic, sexual, offensive, commercial and disputed idea remains in the raw layer; the record separates attributed memory, critical analogy, collector claims, operational violence and unverified Marvel/The Hundreds leads.
